why: When an activity feels difficult or threatening, manageable practice can help build capacity and confidence without treating every symptom as damage.

slides.title: Start With the Goal
slides.content: Choose an activity that matters to you. The goal is meaningful participation—not completing an arbitrary exercise perfectly.

slides.title: Find a Manageable Version
slides.content: Adjust the range, load, speed, duration, support, or environment until the task feels workable and safe for your current plan.

slides.title: Symptoms Are One Input
slides.content: Notice symptoms alongside control, confidence, function, and recovery afterward. A sensation does not automatically mean harm, but important changes should not be ignored.

slides.title: Progress From the Response
slides.content: Repeat, increase, maintain, or temporarily reduce the challenge using your goals, response, and clinician's guidance—not a universal percentage.

slides.title: Try This Today
slides.content: Choose one meaningful movement and make it one step more manageable. Record what you expected, what happened, and what you would adjust next time.

title: Build confidence through practice
